findings.description: The inline user policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's key would permit reading or destroying any S3 data, launching/terminating any EC2 instance, and privilege escalation via lambda:UpdateFunctionCode or passing/using instance profiles.

A permanent IAM access key/secret pair is generated for a user holding wildcard ec2/s3/lambda/cloudwatch permissions. No pgp_key is supplied, so the plaintext secret and ses_smtp_password_v4 are persisted in the Terraform state file; anyone with state read access obtains standing, non-rotating high-privilege credentials.

findings.issue_category: static IAM user instead of role
findings.description: A long-lived IAM user with a static access key and an inline near-admin policy is used instead of a role issuing temporary credentials, with no permissions boundary or MFA condition enforced. This maximises the blast radius and duration of any credential exposure.

The 'secret' output emits access key material from the module and is not marked sensitive. Because no pgp_key was set on the access key, encrypted_secret is unpopulated and the surrounding pattern exports credential attributes that are persisted in state and can be printed in CLI/CI logs.
